internal.title: Incident Report: Checkout Service Error Rate Spike Due to Payment Service Flag
internal.body:
At 11:07 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. The investigation identified that the root cause was an error injection in the payment service, specifically linked to the paymentFailure flag being enabled at 100%. This flag caused the payment service error rate to spike to 100%, directly impacting the checkout service.

The mitigation involved disabling the paymentFailure flag at 11:27 UTC after approval, which led to immediate recovery and normalization of error rates in the checkout service. The incident was resolved promptly with no further impact.

Timeline:
- 11:07:34: Alert received for high error rate in checkout.
- 11:27:18: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection due to paymentFailure flag.
- 11:27:23: Flag disabled after approval.
- 11:27:23: Recovery verified with error rates returning to normal.

Lessons learned include the critical impact of feature flags on dependent services and the importance of rapid flag rollback procedures.

Our team identified the cause and resolved it by disabling a problematic feature flag. The service has since returned to normal operation. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

action_items: Review and improve feature flag deployment and rollback procedures.
Enhance monitoring and alerting on critical feature flags to detect issues earlier.
